# configdirector_environment (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    configdirector = {
      source  = "ConfigDirector/configdirector"
      version = "~> 0.2"
    }
  }
}

provider "configdirector" {}

resource "configdirector_project" "example" {
  name = "Environment Example"
  slug = "environment-example"
}

# Projects already come with "test" and "production" environments;
# configdirector_environment adds any others you need beyond those two.
resource "configdirector_environment" "staging" {
  project_id = configdirector_project.example.id
  name       = "Staging"
  slug       = "staging"
  color      = "purple"
  live       = false
}

# "live" marks an environment as serving real traffic (as opposed to a
# pre-release environment like staging above) - it's informational only and
# doesn't otherwise change how Terraform manages the environment.
resource "configdirector_environment" "canary" {
  project_id = configdirector_project.example.id
  name       = "Canary"
  slug       = "canary"
  color      = "yellow"
  live       = true
}

output "staging_environment_id" {
  value = configdirector_environment.staging.id
}
```

## Deletion protection

While deletion protection is on for an environment, destroying it fails with an error that says where to turn it off, and so does destroying its project. Deletion protection is turned on and off in the ConfigDirector dashboard, and Terraform reads it as `deletion_protection`. An environment the dashboard creates as live, such as the Production environment of a project created there, starts with it on; one Terraform creates starts with it off.

Add `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` to a protected environment to keep Terraform from planning its destroy:

```terraform
import {
  to = configdirector_project.storefront
  id = "storefront"
}

import {
  to = configdirector_environment.production
  id = "storefront/production"
}

resource "configdirector_project" "storefront" {
  name = "Storefront"
  slug = "storefront"
}

resource "configdirector_environment" "production" {
  project_id = configdirector_project.storefront.id
  name       = "Production"
  slug       = "production"
  color      = "red"
  live       = true

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `color` (String)
- `live` (Boolean)
- `name` (String)
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project this environment belongs to.
- `slug` (String)

### Read-Only

- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Whether deletion protection is on. It is set in the ConfigDirector dashboard; while on, destroying this resource fails. Pair it with `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` to keep Terraform from planning the destroy.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = configdirector_environment.staging
  id = "environment-example/staging"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <project_id_or_slug>/<environment_id_or_slug> - both halves accept either
# form: the project, its UUID or its slug; the environment, its UUID or its
# slug, e.g. "test"/"production" (the two environments every project is
# created with).
terraform import configdirector_environment.staging environment-example/staging
```
